messages:
sasha: Noticing a weird session-fence leak when the routing policy flips during a canary -> prod roll. Clients receive a stale fence token and we end up with orphaned server-side resources. Repro in staging after a route-swap.

mike: Can you paste the minimal logs? Is it the fence-id header or the session cookie that's stale?

sasha: fence-id header. Example from proxy logs (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-18T15:21:02Z] REQ id=abcd123 route=canary -> svcA fence=FENCE:20260318:42
[2026-03-18T15:21:02Z] ROUTE_SWAP id=abcd123 to=prod svc=svcB
[2026-03-18T15:21:02Z] RESP id=abcd123 svcB fence_received=FENCE:20260318:41
```

sasha: Note the fence in resp is older than the outgoing fence; svcB didn't accept new fence so proxy kept the session alive waiting for resume. After N seconds we run into quota duplicates and metric spikes.

anya: Hmm, that sounds like a race where the routing layer drops fence semantics when we do transparent route-swaps. The runtime only understands fence monotonicity if it's propagated in the websocket subprotocol. Do we strip/translate headers during routing? :thinking:

priya: We do canonicalize some headers in the HTTP->WS upgrade path. I suspect the LB shim is replacing fence header with the last-seen value from the route table. That's probably a bug in the sticky-routing cache.

jamie: We should avoid relying on fence being strictly monotonic across route flips. Two actionable options: 1) make routing atomic for in-flight streams (buffer until fence ack) or 2) carry an explicit fence-epoch marker in the stream subprotocol so downstream services can accept newer fences even if their local state is older.

mike: Option 2 seems lighter. Add an "fence-epoch" frame in the WS/SSE init and make the runtime treat it as authoritative. Ops: does this change affect billing/console aggregation? We need telemetry to understand dup-token billing risk.

ops-bot: FYI quota-alert: staging rate-surge detected 03:21. Duplicate session allocations +12% since deploy. See /dashboards/streaming/session-fence for current sampling.

sasha: I prototyped option 2 in a branch. It adds an init frame `{"fence_epoch": 17105}` and runtime will accept if epoch >= local. Works in staging — eliminates orphan keepalive. Patch: github.com/redwood/route/PR/482

priya: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) console UX — the dashboard should show fence-epoch histograms and a small note on route-swap windows, 2) rollout: feature-flag the epoch header to runtime so Dedicated customers can toggle it.

anya: Agree. Also add an end-to-end e2e test that simulates rapid route-swap with older downstream state. We should add a telemetry label `route_swap_reason` so ops can filter spikes by policy type (canary, enforce, emergency).

mike: I'll review the PR. If clean, we can dogfood behind a feature flag in prod canary. Also add a metric for "session_fence_rejected" with sample traces for top 5 tenants.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: PR 482 -> canary. Expected rollout window: 15m. :rocket:

sasha: Thanks — leaving a note in the console rollout doc. After canary, let's confirm no billing duplicates and then enable global. If anyone sees stale fence errors, ping me with trace id.

mike: Quick note: please update the API spec for streaming init frames so SDKs can be updated. devex, can you add a tiny blurb in the streaming quickstart? @devex

priya: I'll add the console card and the telemetry query. Also adding an alert: "sse.fence_epoch_gap > 1" for any tenant with streaming traffic.

jamie: Sounds good. :thumbsup:

sasha: closing loop — will post results after canary run.
